chapter: Faith, Paris life and later years
title: His 1975 heart attack and recovery
summary: He had a heart attack on December 6, 1975, was saved by his wife's quick call, and went back to playing in Germany by February; Dance ends on his satisfying life.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, listen -- and then you just pick and choose -- you have some students that you accept.
Yeah. I feel that they --
You just don't want to do too much.
No, I don't want to -- well, then I had this heart attack in 1975.
Oh, I didn't know that.
Uh-huh. I had a -- you know, an infarctus, as we call it.
Oh.
They call it infraction in the United States.
Yeah.
A myocardial infraction (PHONETIC).
Take you by surprise then, huh?
Oh, it did. But the doctor said it's a time limit that really saves your life, if you get to the hospital in time, so it won't ingraide and get too --
So the damage isn't too bad.
That's right. So I escaped with no damage hardly at all, you know.
I see.
Because the quick thinking of my wife got this ambulance there and I was lying in the hospital in 15 minutes.
No kidding. She realized what happened.

Oh, she realized right away. She called her doctor and said, 'He's having pains here.' He said, 'That's his heart. Call the ambulance.' Boom, and I was right in the hospital. So I stayed in [intensive] extensive care for about 11 days, and now they gave me an anti-coagulant, you know. So now -- in December he's going to take me off of that. So I go once a month for x-ray and what they call unintelligible, which is to see if your blood is flowing regularly and smoothly, you know.
Yeah.

So once a month I have to go there. So I was there a couple of weeks ago and he said, "You're doing fine." So I told him I was going to the States, so he says, "Well, when you come back I'll give you another examination, to see how you're doing." But everytime I go he says, "My, you're doing fine." So I feel good.
And the only thing is you know you're not supposed to do too much now.
No.
That you shouldn't overload yourself.

No. Well, it happened the 6th of December, 1975, so I didn't work all December, January, and I started back a little bit in the month of February. That's when I went to Germany. I said, "Oh, I have to play. I can't be sitting around like this. I'll forget how to play." So I went to Germany with Dusko Goykovich's band, and I stayed up there awhile, and got myself -- I felt good and got back to playing again.
Yeah.
So I've been going ever since. It's been very --
Well, that's wonderful.
I was very lucky about that.
That's very wonderful. So really that -- we can end on a note like that, because --
Uh-huh.
Because you have succeeded in establishing a very attractive, satisfying life for yourself.
Well, I think so. I think so.
Yeah. You've done what belonged to you, you know.
